title: The Three-Qubit Bit-Flip Code
summary: The three-qubit bit-flip code, syndrome measurement and the threshold.
objectives: Spread one qubit over three with two CNOT gates and explain why this is not copying
Read the position of a single bit flip from two parities, without measuring the data qubits
Correct a single flip with gates controlled by the syndrome
Work out the logical error rate 3p² − 2p³ and the range of p where the code helps
mission: A bit flip is the simplest error to fight, and three qubits are enough to do it. Encode qubit 0 into three qubits (encode), store the syndrome in two ancillas without measuring the data qubits, and correct the flipped qubit (recover). The logical state must survive an X error on any one of the three qubits, for any input state. The code must also reproduce the theory for noise: when every qubit suffers a bit flip with probability p = 0.1, the logical state survives with probability 1 − 3p² + 2p³ = 0.972, against 0.9 for an unprotected qubit.

prediction.question: The input is |0⟩, encoded as |000⟩, and X errors hit qubits 0 and 1. What do the three data qubits hold after the recovery?
options: |111⟩, the logical |1⟩: the recovery flips qubit 2 as well
|000⟩: the syndrome sees both flips and undoes them
A mixture of |000⟩ and |111⟩, because the syndrome cannot say which qubit to fix
prediction.explanation: The parities of qubits 0, 1 and of qubits 1, 2 are 0 and 1, the syndrome of a single flip on qubit 2. The syndrome is a definite pair of bits, so the recovery applies X to qubit 2 with certainty, and all three qubits are flipped: a logical X, not a mixture. The code corrects one flip, not two.

hints: The encoded state has to be entangled, not copied. What happens to |000⟩ and |111⟩ if you apply a CNOT from qubit 0 to qubit 1 and another from qubit 0 to qubit 2 to α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ on qubit 0?

The syndrome is two parities. Ancilla 3 gets CNOTs from qubits 0 and 1, ancilla 4 gets CNOTs from qubits 1 and 2. Work out the two bits for X on each data qubit: they must be different for the three qubits (10, 11 and 01).

For the correction, qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 4, target]) fires when both ancillas are 1. For a pattern with a 0, apply qml.PauliX to that ancilla before and after the Toffoli. Once recover() fixes every single flip, the noisy case follows by itself.

messages.ok: The logical state survives any single bit flip. With bit-flip noise p = 0.1 on every qubit, the fidelity is {fidelity}, against {bare} for an unprotected qubit.
messages.no_circuit: Define the QNode circuit() on a default.mixed device with 5 qubits.
messages.wrong_qubits: The code uses 3 data qubits and 2 ancillas, 5 in total, but the circuit has {count}.
messages.encode_wrong: With no error at all the final state is not α|000⟩ + β|111⟩ (fidelity {fidelity}). Either the encoding is off, or the recovery acts when the syndrome is 00 and spoils a good state.
messages.single_fail: With the error {error} the logical state was not recovered (fidelity {fidelity}). Probably one syndrome pattern corrects the wrong qubit: check which qubit each pair of parities points to.
messages.noisy_mismatch: Every single flip is corrected, but with bit-flip noise p = 0.1 the fidelity is {fidelity} instead of {expected}. Check that the noise reaches all three data qubits before the recovery and that the recovery itself is noiseless.

challenge.mission: The recovery of the mission spends two ancilla qubits and four CNOT gates on a syndrome. The data qubits can carry the syndrome themselves: if you undo the encoding, a flip of qubit 0 leaves 1 on both qubits 1 and 2, and no other single flip does, so one Toffoli gate decides whether qubit 0 needs correcting. Write recover_compact(), a recovery that does this using wires 0, 1 and 2 only. Afterwards qubit 0 holds the input state and the other two hold the syndrome, so this recovery decodes: unlike recover(), it does not leave the data in the code space, and the validator does not ask for that. The validator takes your encode(), applies an X error to each of the three qubits in turn (and none), then your recover_compact(), for five random input states, and requires that qubit 0 ends in the input state and that no gate acts on wires 3 or 4.
hints: Run the encoding backwards on α|000⟩ + β|111⟩, and again on the same state after an X on qubit 1. Where do the 0 and the 1 of the input end up in each case?
Once the two CNOT gates are undone, qubit 0 is already right unless it was the one flipped. Work out qubits 1 and 2 for no error and for X on qubit 0, 1 and 2: only one of the four cases gives 11.
The gate that fires only on 11 is qml.Toffoli(wires=[1, 2, 0]), and it goes after the two CNOT gates. Each CNOT gate is its own inverse.

messages.ch_ok: Qubit 0 is back in the input state after an X error on any of the three qubits, and after no error, for five random inputs, with no gate on an ancilla wire. The lowest fidelity was {worst}.
messages.ch_no_encode: Define encode() as in the mission: the challenge starts from the same code.
messages.ch_error: Running encode() and recover_compact() raised an error ({detail}). Check that every gate acts on wires 0, 1 and 2 and has the right number of wires.
messages.ch_ancilla: recover_compact acts on wire {wires}. In this version the data qubits do the whole job and the syndrome has no qubits of its own, so only wires 0, 1 and 2 are allowed.
messages.ch_idle: With no error, qubit 0 does not end in the input state (fidelity {fidelity}). Probably the Toffoli gate fires when it should not, or the encoding is not undone before it: the two CNOT gates from qubit 0 come first.
messages.ch_fail: With {error}, qubit 0 does not end in the input state (fidelity {fidelity}). Probably the Toffoli gate acts before the encoding is undone, or its controls are not qubits 1 and 2: after the decoding, only a flip of qubit 0 puts a 1 on both.
